executiveSummary: The week's net movement was toward escalation on two fronts and hardening of a structural constraint. A U.S.–Iran maritime confrontation in the Strait of Hormuz escalated to direct fires (ballistic missiles at U.S. Navy units; tanker strikes), opening a new high-consequence thread. In Ukraine, a narrow 3-day capital-strike pause gave way mid-week to a reported 30-day halt on strikes against energy infrastructure — a category-bounded, still-fragile de-escalation rather than a ceasefire. On the industrial side, China's rare-earth leverage sharpened from broad controls to entity-list targeting of the very U.S. firms building domestic magnet substitution. Cyber risk concentrated on trust-boundary and AI-infrastructure components (CISA KEV adds) plus a reported mass identity-vendor breach. CMMC remained paused-but-binding. For an enterprise-tech/security leader the week's throughline is assurance under pressure: identity, edge, and AI-infrastructure exposure rising while compliance timing stays uncertain and materials risk deepens.
whatChanged: New thread opened: U.S.–Iran direct fires in the Strait of Hormuz (5–6 Sep), a step-change from gray-zone tanker pressure.
Ukraine diplomacy shifted from a 3-day capital-strike pause to a reported 30-day energy-infrastructure strike halt after a Trump–Putin call (7 Sep).
China's rare-earth posture moved from broad export controls to entity-list targeting of MP Materials and USA Rare Earth (June 2026 measure surfacing in analysis).
CISA KEV additions concentrated on edge/identity (SonicWall SMA1000), CI/CD (JFrog Artifactory), and AI-gateway (LiteLLM) components.
A reported 153M+ driver's-license/ID breach at an identity-verification vendor entered criminal markets (FBI investigating; vendor unconfirmed).
DoD leadership churn: Army Secretary Driscoll resigned amid modernization clashes.
